subject: Implementation & Migration Questionnaire — QuantumPay RFI
messages:

Subject: RFI: Implementation & Migration Questionnaire

Hi Sean / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the RFI template. We're attaching the Implementation & Migration questionnaire with a few custom items specific to our payments stack (PCI-adjacent data flows, KMS key separation, and canary rollback SLAs). Our procurement window is tight — we need completed responses by EOD 2026-06-26 to align with our supplier evaluation.

Top concerns we expect your answers on:
- Proposed migration timeline (staging -> canary -> cutover)
- Integration steps for SSO (IdP via SAML) and billing events
- Rollback & fallback procedures (how quickly we can revert to previous model/endpoint)
- Data residency / retention enforcement and evidence for SOC2 controls
- Expected downtime or client-side session impacts during cutover

Please mark any items that require a technical change or additional security review.

Attaching: QuantumPay_RFI_Implem_Questions.xlsx (15 questions, tabbed)

Appreciate a concise plan + checklist we can put into our procurement doc.

Best,
Liz Chen
Head of Platform Integrations

Subject: Re: RFI: Implementation & Migration Questionnaire

Liz — thanks, got the spreadsheet. We filled the RFI inline and are attaching a short implementation playbook that maps to each QuantumPay question. High-level summary below; see attached: QP_Onboarding_Sequence_v2.xlsx and redwood-deployment-architecture.pdf.

Summary proposal (staging -> production):
1) Prep & access (Week 0–1): SAML integration test users, KMS key handshake, network allowlists.
2) Staging validation (Week 2): End-to-end shadow routing for a subset of traffic; run prompt sets and monitor latency/quality regressions.
3) Canary (Week 3): Gradual ramp beginning at 1% traffic → 5% → 20% across 3 business days with automated rollback triggers.
4) Cutover (Week 4): 100% routing switch + 72h observability window and cost/latency audit.

Key integration steps (short):
- Deploy private VPC peering and route tables; confirm egress rules for telemetry.
- SAML exchange + test assertion flow; default session TTLs documented.
- KV-cache warm-up run using bulk prefix load during staging (details in attachment).
- Billing event webhook and idempotency best practices.

Canary strategy (automated):
- Metric gates: p95 latency, error-rate (>1.5% triggers rollback), model output regression score (custom prompt-set).
- Fallback: route to a smaller, faster variant or previous model digest; preserve sessions via sticky routing for 10 minutes.

Rollback window: immediate automated rollback on metric breach, or manual rollback with confirmed DB/offset snapshot in <2 hours.

Dependencies & blockers:
- IdP team to provide SAML metadata and test users by day 3 of Prep.
- Procurement acceptance of the latency SLO defined in the attached doc.

Let us know if the timelines look tight; we can propose an accelerated 2-week pilot if QuantumPay can allocate a staging testbed and 10% shadow capacity.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: QP_Onboarding_Sequence_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-deployment-architecture.pdf (diagram)]

Subject: Re: Implementation & Migration Questionnaire — technical clarifications

David — good questions. Below are concrete answers and the metrics we'll use during canary testing.

KV-cache warm-up
- Recommended: synthetic prefix load for initial warm-up + backfill from historical session keys. Synthetic load is safe and reproducible; backfill only for non-sensitive session metadata. Expected memory: ~0.45GB per 10k 32-token avg sessions on our standard quantized profile (varies with model size).

Session continuity & rollback behavior
- Mirror-for-10-min option: we can mirror traffic to Redwood while continuing to serve from the incumbent endpoint for active sessions; this avoids user-visible drops. After 10 minutes of mirror validation (latency/quality gates), we start sticky routing for new sessions.
- Rollback approach: immediate metric-triggered route removal for new traffic; existing sticky sessions preserved for their TTL (default 30 min) and then drained. If you require zero interruption, we recommend the mirror-for-10-min then soft-cutover path.

Canary metric gates (proposed concrete thresholds)
- Latency (p95): +15% over baseline tolerated; >25% triggers rollback.
- Error rate: >1.5% absolute error-rate triggers rollback.
- Quality regression: >3% degrade on your acceptance prompt-set (we'll run the same test harness) triggers review; >6% triggers automated rollback.
- Token-cost spike: sudden >40% increase in per-turn token consumption (unexpected token inflation) triggers immediate pause and analysis.

Rollout cadence (detailed)
- Day 0–2: Mirror traffic (no user cutover) — smoke tests & production prompt-set evaluation.
- Day 3: 1% production traffic (monitor 24–48h).
- Day 5: 5% production traffic (monitor 48–72h).
- Day 8: 20% production traffic (monitor 72h).
- Day 12: 50% production traffic (monitor 72h).
- Day 15: 100% cutover + 72h elevated monitoring.

Deliverables we will provide by the end of Prep:
- Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft (HubSpot link to be provided)
- SAML test user list & expected assertion logs
- KMS key exchange checklist

If these thresholds look acceptable we will add them into the RFI responses and the MAP.

-Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
